events.text: The Taj Mahal mausoleum is completed for Shah Jahan at Agra
The Sydney Opera House is formally opened on Bennelong Point
The Colosseum is completed in Rome under the emperor Titus
Hagia Sophia is completed as the cathedral of Constantinople

reveal.explanation: The Colosseum was finished in Rome in AD 80 and Hagia Sophia followed more than four centuries later in 537. Shah Jahan's mausoleum at Agra was completed in 1648, and the Sydney Opera House opened on Bennelong Point in 1973.

sources.excerpt: Construction began under the Emperor Vespasian in 72 and was completed in AD 80 under his successor and heir, Titus.

The last of three church buildings to be successively erected on the site by the Eastern Roman Empire, it was completed in AD 537, becoming the world's largest interior space and among the first to employ a fully pendentive dome.
Construction of the mausoleum was completed in 1648, although work on other parts of the complex continued for another five years.
The Sydney Opera House was formally opened by Queen Elizabeth II, on 20 October 1973.
